Roofing in Argyle, Texas

Argyle mixes horse acreage with master-planned streets, and hail does not care which. Call one free number, any hour, to reach an independent roofing company that takes Argyle calls.

Call (469) 649-7066 Argyle's contractor rule
  1. Home
  2. Service Areas
  3. Argyle

Small town, big hail

Roofing in Argyle, TX comes up most after hail. On March 26, 2017, a storm that lasted about five minutes left roofs across Argyle damaged badly enough that many had to be replaced outright, according to the Argyle High student newspaper, The Talon News. Car windows were smashed all over town.

Argyle is a small town about six miles southwest of Denton. It counted 4,403 residents in the 2020 census, and the Census Bureau estimated 5,859 by mid-2023, so it is growing quickly. Homes range from horse properties with pasture, stalls and arenas to newer houses in master-planned communities such as Harvest and Canyon Falls that carry Argyle addresses.

DFW Expert Roofers is a free phone line, not a contractor. Calling it connects you with an independent, locally owned roofing company that takes Argyle calls. That company looks at the roof, house and barn alike, and gives you its own price.

Argyle's contractor rule: register and show $500,000 in coverage

Most towns ask for a contractor's insurance certificate. Argyle puts a number on it.

Who must register

All contractors, before performing services within town limits. Registration is yearly. A homeowner doing work on their own home does not register but must still follow the codes.

What they file

A registration application, a valid trade license or a driver's license where there is no state trade license (the case for roofers), and a certificate of insurance with at least $500,000 in coverage.

What it costs the roofer

$125 for the first registration, then $50 for each yearly renewal, per the town's fee schedule.

Where to ask

The Permits Department at 308 Denton Street, open weekdays 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., phone 940-464-7273. Applications run through the town's iWorQ portal.

On permits, the town's rule is broad: a permit is needed before new construction, an addition, or the alteration or repair of an existing building. Its FAQ list of common permit projects does not mention roofs, so call the permits office before a re-roof and get a clear answer for your address.

Hail Argyle has seen

WhenWhat was reported
March 26, 2017A short, intense hailstorm damaged roofs, windows and cars in Argyle; many roofs needed full replacement.
June 11, 2023NBC DFW collected reader photos of very large hail from Argyle and neighboring Flower Mound that Sunday evening.
March 14, 2024Storm report listings show hail about 2.5 inches across near Argyle, nine months after the June storm.

Hail days that close together can complicate an insurance claim, because the insurer may ask which storm caused which damage. Keep dated photos after each storm and write down the date you first noticed a problem. Then ask your insurer how it handles damage from more than one event.

Leave the roof to the roofer. A wet or storm-hit roof is slippery, and damaged decking can give way, so keep off it and keep the ladder put away. Stay clear of any downed power line and report it to Oncor or your local electric utility, or call 911. Inside, pull furniture and electronics away from the drip, set out a bucket or towels, and keep everyone out of a room where the ceiling is sagging. Take photos from the yard and from inside, then call your insurance company and a roofer.

Acreage roofs need a wider look

On a property with a barn, a shop building and a house, a hailstorm rarely hits only one roof. When you call, mention every structure you want checked so the roofing company can plan its visit. Ask whether it handles both shingle and metal roofs, how it documents damage to outbuildings, and whether your insurance policy lists those buildings at all. Some policies treat barns and other structures differently from the home, so read yours or ask your agent.

In a master-planned neighborhood the questions shift. HOA design rules can limit shingle colors and styles, so ask the HOA what is approved before signing. Under section 202.011 of the Texas Property Code, an HOA has limited power to block certain impact-resistant or energy-efficient shingles, a point worth raising with the roofer and the HOA together.

Ask an Argyle roofer

  • Are you registered with the Town of Argyle this year, and can your insurer send me the certificate you filed?
  • Is my property inside town limits, and what permit, if any, will you pull?
  • Will you inspect the barn and outbuildings on the same visit?
  • Which storm date do your photos and notes tie the damage to?
  • Do you install metal as well as shingles, and how do the warranties differ?

Your deductible is yours to pay. The Texas Department of Insurance warns that a contractor may not waive your deductible, rebate it, or pad the estimate to cover it, and that a contract of $1,000 or more paid with insurance money must include a notice that you owe the deductible. Your insurer may ask for proof you paid it. A contractor also may not act as a public adjuster on a property it works on or may work on. If a roofer offers to "take care of" the deductible, hire someone else.

Roofing questions from Argyle

Do roofing companies in Argyle TX have to register with the town?

Yes, inside town limits. Argyle requires every contractor to register before doing work in the town, renew each year, and file a certificate of insurance showing at least $500,000 in coverage. The first registration is $125 and renewals are $50. Ask the roofer for its registration, and see the roofer checking guide for the other items to request, since Texas has no state roofing license.

Is an Argyle town permit required for a roof replacement?

The town says permits are required before new construction, additions, alterations or repairs of existing buildings, but its list of common permit projects does not name roofing. Rather than guess, call the Permits Department at 940-464-7273 or check the iWorQ portal checklists before the work starts, and ask your roofer to confirm what it has filed. Homes outside town limits may fall under other rules.

Is my Argyle address inside the Town of Argyle?

Not necessarily. Argyle mailing addresses spread beyond the town itself, and listings show some Argyle addresses served by Denton ISD or Northwest ISD. The town's registration and permit rules apply within town limits. Your property tax statement or the town permits office can tell you which local government covers your lot, which matters when the roofer pulls permits.

Can I get a metal roof on my barn and house in Argyle?

Many acreage properties around Argyle have barns and outbuildings, and metal is a common choice for them. Whether it suits the house depends on the structure, the look you want and any deed restrictions or HOA rules on your lot. A roofing company can price both and explain the trade-offs. The metal roofing page covers panel types and what to ask.
